answer: When agents share a payment vault or exhibit correlated transaction timing, the network performs kin-linking: grouping identities into a single economic entity. Each agent must post collateral proportional to its claimed independence. If two agents both bid on the same jetty lease within milliseconds, or withdraw from a shared ocean of liquidity using the same root key, the system treats them as one actor and sums their stakes. An attacker spawning ten sonnet-writing bots from one wallet now needs ten times the bond, turning linear Sybil creation into quadratic cost.
